Titled zone card

.dr .dr-zone · __title · __sub · components/rows.css · kit specimen

Anatomy

Drone type

Which drone does your order

  1. 1.dr-zoneThe card: --bg-surface, radius 16, a 16 inset on all four sides. Selected as .dr .dr-zone (0-2-0), because the base .dr fieldset{ padding: 0 } is 0-1-1 and a zone may be a fieldset.
  2. 2.dr-zone__titleThe question the card asks, 17/600 in --text-primary, 14.37:1. It names the group through aria-labelledby.
  3. 3.dr-zone__subOne line on what the answer is for, 13/400 in --text-muted, 5.95:1, 4 under the title, read through aria-describedby.
  4. 4.dr-picksThe control group, 20 under the subtitle (16 under 390px). It gives up its own ground, radius and inset to the card and does not move.

Variants and sizes

Inventory rows: Titled zone card.

States

No state of its own: the card names a group and holds other components. Its choices take the checkbox states and its fields take the field states.

When to use

The titled zone card is the card a group of entered data opens with: every card in the product that holds data the user enters, sorted into categories. It stands on 10 files, 14 cards: the filters drawer on the four listings files (Drone type), account-edit (Personal details · Payment method · Language · Appearance · Notifications), payment, payment-aerial and payment-inspection (Card), order-setup-inspection (Subject) and operator-profile-setup (Service specializations). 13 of the 14 cards carry a subtitle; the one on operator-profile-setup has a title only and no aria-describedby. The title and subtitle are the card's own, inside its surface: a zone label names a region of the screen and sits outside any surface.

It does not go on an entry group that is a plain list (order-setup, report-issue, contact-support, rate; order-setup-inspection's Subject is the exception), on a navigation group (account), on an upload card that has its own title, or on the order and operator cards, which display rather than collect. What it costs is height: +66 per card for the two lines and the 20 gap. Green spent: 0px².

The title is the question as a noun (Drone type, Personal details); the subtitle says what the answer is for, in the user's words (What the operator needs to reach you). Titles are <p>, not headings: WCAG 2.4.10 is AAA and the target is AA. A <legend> is not used, because it renders in the fieldset's border region and takes the 16 inset with it.
